problem: Reactive VLA navigation policies lack long-horizon look-ahead, while JEPA world-model planners (MPPI/CEM) start from an uninformed Gaussian over a high-dimensional action space, converging slowly and getting stuck in local minima.
motivation: Instruction-conditioned goal-image navigation needs both language grounding and multi-step reasoning about consequences. A finetuned policy gives semantically informed action proposals, while a latent world model can evaluate them over longer horizons; combining the two should make planning cheaper and more accurate.
key_idea: Use the action distribution (mean and std of diffusion samples) from a finetuned Octo policy to warm-start MPPI planning over a language-agnostic JEPA world model that is scored by latent distance to the goal image.
insight: Warm-starting gives the best trajectory-level position accuracy: with V-JEPA-2, ATE XY RMSE is 1.65 m versus 1.72 for Octo and 1.87 for uninformed MPPI. The Octo-WM ablation (best-of-N policy samples scored by the world model, with no MPPI refinement) recovers most of the gain, so filtering by the world model matters most and MPPI refinement adds a little more. Uninformed MPPI is worst on position but best on heading, suggesting the embedding-space cost regularizes heading.
method: Policy prior: an Octo-Small policy with a frozen DINOv2 ViT-S or V-JEPA-2 ViT-L encoder plus a learnable projection, finetuned on CAST with T5 language and a DDPM diffusion head; N_pi=4 action-chunk samples are drawn.

Coordinate transform: global-frame displacements are rotated into the world model's local body frame by accumulating headings, then normalized to [-1,1]. The mean mu_0 and std sigma_0 (clamped to [0.01,0.05]) of the samples become the MPPI initialization.

JEPA world model: a ViT predictor with frame-causal attention and AdaLN action conditioning on frozen-encoder latents, trained with a multi-step rollout MSE loss and truncated BPTT. It is language-agnostic.

Policy-guided MPPI: J=4 iterations, N=32 samples, K=4 elites, lambda=0.8. Candidates are scored by terminal latent distance to the goal embedding, the elite-weighted mean and std are updated, and one elite is sampled and executed.
Encoder study: four policy/WM encoder pairings (DINOv2 and V-JEPA-2, same-encoder and cross-encoder) are trained. Only same-encoder results are reported in the tables.
Baselines: Octo alone, default MPPI (mean 0, std sigma_max), and Octo-WM (pick the policy sample with the lowest world-model cost).

setting.backbone: Octo-Small (fine-tuned, frozen DINOv2 ViT-S or V-JEPA-2 ViT-L encoder) + JEPA ViT world model predictor trained separately
setting.training_data: CAST navigation dataset (with counterfactual language-action augmentation), used for both policy and world model
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB + goal image + language instruction
setting.action_space: 4-D local-frame displacement/heading chunks (dx, dy, sin dphi, cos dphi), horizon 8
setting.simulator: none; offline evaluation on CAST validation episodes
setting.privileged: none (goal image is given as part of the task)

numbers.evidence: Table 1: DINOv2 ViT-S on CAST validation episodes, PiJEPA row
Table 2: V-JEPA-2 ViT-L on CAST validation episodes, PiJEPA row

numbers_note: Only offline trajectory-error metrics (ATE/RPE) on CAST validation; no SR/SPL and no simulator or real-robot benchmark, despite the abstract's 'real-world navigation tasks' claim. The CAST-val tables do not match any canonical benchmark, so they are recorded under 'other'. Cross-encoder variants are not tabulated.
results: PiJEPA has the lowest ATE XY RMSE in both encoder settings (1.78 m with DINOv2, 1.65 m with V-JEPA-2), beating Octo (1.98 / 1.72), uninformed MPPI (1.85 / 1.87) and Octo-WM (1.80 / 1.67). Gains are small in absolute terms. MPPI is best on heading metrics, and Octo-WM narrowly wins final position with V-JEPA-2 (2.87 vs 2.88). Total inference is about 2.48 s (2.13 s policy diffusion + 0.35 s MPPI).
limitations: Evaluated only offline on CAST validation trajectory error (no closed-loop success rate, no real-robot or simulator navigation), and the improvements over Octo and Octo-WM are marginal.
The world model can stall, predicting near-identical latents regardless of action, and ambiguous instructions such as 'Follow the building' still lead to failure.
Policy diffusion sampling dominates latency (~2.1 s), and the world model is language-agnostic, so instruction grounding depends entirely on the policy prior.
